reviewCommentsList.author: Copilot
reviewCommentsList.body:
The new fixCleanup3_5_0 check for `deletedVault_` ("vault deletion must not create or modify another vault") is placed after the early return for `txnType == ttVAULT_DELETE`. As a result, a malformed `ttVAULT_DELETE` that both deletes a vault and also creates/modifies another vault will never hit the intended diagnostic and will instead be reported as "vault deletion succeeded without deleting a vault".

Move the `deletedVault_` check above the `ttVAULT_DELETE` early-return so the stricter rule is enforced (and the correct diagnostic is emitted) for VaultDelete as well.

Adds null `SLE` checks in directory iteration callbacks for `NoRippleCheck` and `GatewayBalances`.

prs.body:
## Context of the change: 

https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/pull/6029# 

In this PR, @oleks-rip made a fix to test the validity of txnDB (transaction database connection object) pointer before dereferencing it. In this case, the config suggested that txn tables are not being used and hence the txn DB connection object should be null. But it was still being dereferenced without confirming its validity. Config:

[ledger_tx_tables]
use_tx_tables = 0

The pattern followed in this PR was to check the config, if the config suggests that db connection should be created, it must have been created and is valid. So, no explicit check on the actual db connection object is required. As per code review feedback an additional check on the txnDB object was added, failing this would throw a runtime error.

Apparently, this pattern (of relying on the config settings and not on validity of actual objects) is being followed at multiple places. We only check the config to assume the validity of the corresponding objects. As shared in the PR comments, at many places we don’t explicitly check the validity of the connection or other objects before using it. Moreover, if the object is invalid, there seem to be no guidelines around how to handle it? Should the program just throw a runtime error and exit? Should the program retry (how many times?) to create a valid txn db connection object? Should the code throw and log an exception and cancel the transaction that’s supposed to be written to the db? Should we initiate a re-sync since this write failed? Should the app be relaunched and so that it can re-initialise?
We need set proper guidelines on this and document the behaviour.

Please check PR for more details on the change and the related discussion.

The objective of this ticket is to start a discussion around this and finalize the behavior we want going forward. This will require updating code to follow agreed upon guidelines and fix any potential bugs.

We recently merged a refactor to `develop` that enables clang-tidy's `readability-identifier-naming`. Your branch now has heavy conflicts that are largely mechanical. Below is a workflow that aligns your branch's naming with develop _before_ merging, which should minimize the merge conflicts.

## One-time setup

If you don't already have clang-tidy working in your env, on macOS:

```bash
brew install llvm@21

```

## Workflow on your branch (before merging develop)

**1. Grab the new `.clang-tidy` from develop without pulling anything else.** Sync your fork on GitHub first, then:

```bash
git remote -v   # should show 'upstream' among others; if not:
# git remote set-url upstream git@github.com:XRPLF/rippled.git
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/develop -- .clang-tidy
```

**2. Reconfigure conan/cmake so `compile_commands.json` is fresh.**

```bash
git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD upstream/develop) HEAD \
```

```bash
cmake --build build -j8
git commit -am "refactor: Align identifier naming with develop"
```

**5. Now merge develop:**

```bash
git merge upstream/develop
```

prs.body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Two additions to the destination checks in `VaultWithdraw`, both gated behind
`fixCleanup3_4_0`. A withdrawal out of a private vault to a third party now
requires both the submitter and the destination to be members of the vault's
permissioned domain. A withdrawal to a pseudo-account is refused with
`tecPSEUDO_ACCOUNT` instead of a misleading `tecNO_PERMISSION`.

### Context of Change

**Permissioned domain.** A private vault restricts who may take part in it, but
`VaultWithdraw` only ever checked that the destination was allowed to hold the
underlying asset, through `requireAuth`. There was no domain check anywhere in
the withdrawal path, so a participant could withdraw to an account the domain
owner never admitted and the funds left the domain. `VaultDeposit` already
applies the equivalent check on the way in, and both callers now share one
helper, `checkVaultDomain`, which reads the domain from the share issuance. The
callers differ only in how they treat an expired credential: the deposit path
tolerates it because `doApply` deletes it, the withdrawal path has no such step
and keeps the error.

Two cases deliberately skip the domain check:

- **Withdrawal to self** is never restricted. Losing vault access must not
  strand funds that were already deposited, so redeeming your own shares stays
  available regardless of domain membership.
- **The asset issuer** is always allowed to receive, which keeps the return path
  for frozen assets open. This exemption covers both parties rather than just
  the recipient: otherwise a submitter who had lost domain access could not
  return a frozen asset to its issuer, which is precisely the situation that
  path exists for. Reviewers may want to look closely at this one, it is the one
  judgement call in the change rather than a direct reading of the
  access-control rules.

**Pseudo-accounts.** A pseudo-account is owned by a ledger object and cannot
take part in a user-initiated payout, but nothing in `VaultWithdraw` said so.
The withdrawal was already refused, because every pseudo-account is created
with deposit authorization set, and the resulting `tecNO_PERMISSION` named the
wrong reason. `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` has always returned
`tecPSEUDO_ACCOUNT` for the same case; `VaultWithdraw` was the odd one out. The
check sits ahead of the domain check so a private vault gives the same answer as
a public one, rather than reporting a pseudo-account as lacking domain
membership it can never hold.

Public vaults, `VaultClawback` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` are unaffected by
the domain check. `VaultClawback` sends to the issuer through a separate path
and does not use `sfDestination` at all.

### API Impact

- [ ] Public API: New feature (new methods and/or new fields)
- [ ] Public API: Breaking change (in general, breaking changes should only impact the next api_version)
- [x] `libxrpl` change (any change that may affect `libxrpl` or dependents of `libxrpl`)
- [ ] Peer protocol change (must be backward compatible or bump the peer protocol version)

Consensus-affecting: a withdrawal that succeeds today can return `tecNO_AUTH`
once `fixCleanup3_4_0` is enabled, and one that fails with `tecNO_PERMISSION`
can return `tecPSEUDO_ACCOUNT` instead. Behavior is unchanged while the
amendment is off.

## Test Plan

Two tests in `src/test/app/Vault_test.cpp`, each run twice, with and without
`fixCleanup3_4_0`. Every account in them holds the asset, so anything blocked is
blocked by the check under test alone.

`testVaultWithdrawPrivateDestinationDomain` covers: destination inside the
domain; destination outside it; destination is the issuer; destination is the
vault owner; withdrawal to self with and without an explicit `Destination`; a
submitter who lost domain access withdrawing to self, to a domain member, and to
the issuer; a private vault whose domain has been cleared; and a public vault
paying out to a non-member.

`testVaultWithdrawPseudoAccountDestination` withdraws to another vault's
pseudo-account out of both a public and a private vault, and confirms that
withdrawal to self out of the same vault is untouched.
